title: Efficient Fault-Tolerant Single Qubit Gate Approximation And Universal Quantum Computation Without Using The Solovay-Kit

predicted_errors.error_location: Conclusion (final paragraph): "one obtains a computational efficient method to approximate any single qubit gate to an accuracy of ϵ using O(ϵ log[1/ϵ] log log[1/ϵ] ···) gates"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract and introduction repeatedly state the main result as O(log[1/ϵ] log log[1/ϵ] log log log[1/ϵ] ···) FT gates (no leading ϵ factor), e.g. 'this is possible using O(log[1/ϵ] log log[1/ϵ] log log log[1/ϵ] · · ·) FT gates' (abstract) and 'approximate any SU(2) operator to an accuracy of ε using O(log[1/ε] log log[1/ε] log log log[1/ε] ··· ) gates' (introduction). The conclusion instead introduces an extra multiplicative factor of ϵ, giving O(ϵ log[1/ϵ] log log[1/ϵ] ···), which is a different (and nonsensical, since it would predict the gate count vanishes as ϵ→0) asymptotic scaling that directly contradicts the paper's stated main result.

predicted_errors.error_location: Conclusion: "apply FT implementation to each phase gate with angle of rotation accurate to ϵ log_2(1/ϵ) log_2 log_2(1/ϵ) ··· until log_2 log_2 ··· log_2(1/ϵ) becomes O(1)"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Earlier in the same paragraph the required angular precision is defined as δ ≤ ϵ/⌈log_2(1/ϵ)⌉ (a division by the log-product, i.e. δ shrinks relative to ϵ). The restated precision requirement, 'accurate to ϵ log_2(1/ϵ) log_2 log_2(1/ϵ)···,' uses multiplication instead of division, giving a precision requirement that is looser (larger) than ϵ itself as the log terms grow, which contradicts the earlier (and more sensible) division-based definition of δ and is internally inconsistent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Conclusion: "the gates needed are drawn from the set {H, P(πℓ/2^m) : m, ℓ ∈ Z^+, ℓ < 2^m} where m = ⌈ϵ/ [log_2(1/ϵ) log_2 log_2(1/ϵ)···]⌉"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The integer m sets the angular resolution π/2^m used to approximate an arbitrary phase to precision δ, so m must grow like log_2(1/δ) ~ log_2(1/ϵ) (plus lower-order log-log corrections) as ϵ→0, i.e. m should increase without bound as ϵ shrinks. The given formula m = ⌈ϵ/[log_2(1/ϵ) log_2log_2(1/ϵ)···]⌉ has ϵ in the numerator and a diverging product of logs in the denominator, so as ϵ→0 the ratio →0 and ⌈·⌉ saturates at 1, meaning m never grows — contradicting the requirement that finer angular resolution (larger m) is needed for smaller ϵ.

predicted_errors.error_location: Method section, paragraph on recursion: "I can implement any P(πℓ/2^m) gate in a FT manner ... in O(n) times through the recursion P(πℓ/2^m) ⇐ P(πℓ/2^{m−1}) ⇐ ··· ⇐ P(πℓ/4)"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The recursion doubles the angle in each step starting from P(πℓ/4), so the number of recursive steps needed to reach P(πℓ/2^m) is governed by m (the exponent), not by n (the code length used elsewhere for the O(n^3) Gaussian-elimination cost of computing P(α)_L). Stating the number of recursive FT implementations scales as O(n) conflates two unrelated parameters (code length n vs. recursion depth m), which is inconsistent with the recursive construction described.
